rule.text:
A line passes only if the total excess over the PO price is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500 [1]. Check the 1% figure first: on a small line it is well below ₹500, so the limit is the 1% figure, not ₹500 [2][3].

If the invoice price is lower than the PO price, accept it and pay the invoice price [1]. A line that fails is held as PRICE_VAR and sent to the buyer who raised the PO, who either amends the PO or asks for a credit note [1].

citations.quote: Where the invoice unit price is higher than the PO unit price, the line passes only if the total excess on that line is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500.

citations.section_title: Shadowing notes — a day with a senior processor
citations.quote: Price variance of ₹460 on a ₹30,000 line. 1% of the line is ₹300, so the limit is ₹300, not ₹500. Raised PRICE_VAR.

citations.section_title: Expert interview 1 — Lakshmi Reddy, Senior Processor
citations.quote: They remember five hundred rupees and forget it's the lower of one per cent and five hundred. On a small line, one per cent is much less than five hundred.

citations.section_title: Video 1 — AP 101: the life of an invoice
citations.quote: The tolerance on price is the lower of one per cent of the line and five hundred rupees. Remember that number, five hundred.
